request: Audiophile review: least processed, Wii-faithful audio without risking stability
chain_reviewed: AX DSP HLE (ax_mix.cpp): per-voice polyphase SRC from the bundled DSP coefficient ROM, voice LPF/biquad, volume ramps and dpop as the microcode does. Left unchanged (faithful).
Prime AI DMA (audio.cpp): 32 kHz stereo S16 BE, 32 bytes per 250 us.
AudioBackend: endian/L-R swap only, gain 1, previously SDL 3.4.4 converted 32 kHz S16 to the device's 44.1/48 kHz F32.

measurements.clock_drift_before: queue fell ~6 KB per 80 s (~0.02%), would empty in ~7 min
measurements.clock_follower_5min: rate +200..+285 ppm, queue ~53 ms average, 0 underruns

changes: audio_resampler.h: rational polyphase Kaiser windowed-sinc, 128 taps/phase, cutoff 0.965 of source Nyquist, unity-gain phases, float, no dither; exact 441/320 (44.1 kHz) and 3/2 (48 kHz).

AudioBackend opens the stream in the device's own rate and F32 so SDL performs no conversion; WII_COMPILED_AUDIO_SDL_RESAMPLER=1 restores SDL conversion. Underrun counter via SDL get-callback, logged every 10 s.
AI clock follower: paces the emulated AI DMA (never the samples) by at most +-0.1% from a ~2 s average of the output queue, proportional control, target 60 ms.
MusicAttenuation::TickGuest is inert for RM3E01: it followed Mario Kart nw4r::snd pointers at fixed MKW addresses through Prime RAM and could rewrite unrelated floats.

validation.user: user reports audio sounds good and somewhat clearer

limits: SDL uses WASAPI shared mode; exclusive mode and Windows audio enhancements are outside this runtime.
A device default-format change after startup is handled by SDL conversion until restart.
The guest's own content (32 kHz, 16-bit, AX/FMOD mixing) is unchanged by design.
